utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. For the sake of the record, could we have the appearances, please. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Peter McCloskey and Stefan Waespi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. Michael Karnavas and Suzanna Tomanovic on behalf of Vidoje Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I notice a representative from the legal aid section of the registrar is also present in this courtroom. Sir, would you please be kind enough to identify yourself. MR. VAN DE VLIET: Yes, good afternoon, I am Bas Van De Vliet, I am the acting chief of the Office of Legal Aid and Detention Matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Blagojevic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. For the time being I understand everything that's being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, thank you very much. You may sit down, please. And later on when we are going to discuss something, you may answer the questions from this Bench while seated. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this is a hearing -- this is a special hearing for the Rule 84 bis and 85. As Mr. Blagojevic has made statements on various occasions expressing his desire to testify under oath as well as to make a statement in his case, the Trial Chamber finds it necessary to ensure that Mr. Blagojevic is informed and understands the options available to him and the possible implications of each option. Mr. Blagojevic, when you have raised this issue on previous occasions, the Trial Chamber has consistently advised you that decision to testify under oath is one that must be taken only after careful consideration and with full understanding of the possible consequences or ramifications of testifying. To assist you in making an informed decision, the Trial Chamber has advised you to meet with your counsel, Mr. Karnavas. The Trial Chamber has further advised you that if no such meeting takes place, the Trial Chamber would be in a difficult position to grant your request to testify. I would like to ask some questions to Mr. Blagojevic. And could we go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, as you have not met with Mr. Karnavas, the Trial Chamber will set out for you three options available to you. We will, however, explain each option to you from an objective perspective. Only Mr. Karnavas is in a position to advise you on which option may be most appropriate to you in the circumstances of this case. The three options available to you are: First, to exercise your right to remain silent; secondly, to make a statement under the control of the Trial Chamber, the content of which you will not be examined about; or thirdly, to testify under oath like any other witnesses in this case. In relation to the first option to remain silent, Article 21(4)(g) of the Statute guarantees that you will not be compelled to testify against yourself or to confess guilt. This right is related to the right you enjoyed, to be presumed innocent until proven guilty. The burden is on the Prosecution to prove you guilty beyond a reasonable doubt; it is not upon you to prove that you are innocent. No negative inference will be drawn by this Trial Chamber if you choose to remain silent. Along with your counsel, you should, therefore, carefully consider what evidence is before the Trial Chamber before deciding to add your testimony to the evidence that the Trial Chamber will consider when making its final judgement in your case. The second option, to make an unsworn statement is provided in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, especially Rule 84 bis. While under the exact language of the rule, an unsworn statement is generally made after the opening statement of the parties. The Trial Chamber does not find any reason to deny you the opportunity to make an unsworn statement at a later time. What is meant by making an unsworn statement is that you do not have to make the solemn declaration, although you may if you like make the solemn declaration at the start of your statement, and you should not be examined by either parties or the Bench about the content of the statement. There are no guidelines given for the length of such narrative statement, although the Trial Chamber may limit the length if your statement exceeds a reasonable length. Furthermore, the statement is made under the control of the Trial Chamber. This means, for example, that if necessary to stop you for your protection or for the protection of others at a certain point or in relation to a certain topic, the Trial Chamber can do so. Based on your conduct in the proceedings to date, the Trial Chamber has no reason to believe that you could use your statement to call into question the dignity of the proceedings, but it reminds you of its right and its duty to ensure that the dignity of the proceedings are not called into question. As a statement under Rule 84 bis is generally unsworn and is not subject of cross-examination or inquiry from the Bench, it generally will carry somewhat less weight than the testimony given under oath that is subject to cross-examination and inquiry from the Trial Chamber. The third option available to you is to testify as a witness in your case. Rule 85(C) of the rules specifically allows for you to testify. If you were to testify as a witness, you would be required to take a solemn declaration, like any other witnesses in this trial. It is required that the party calling the witness examine the witness. Therefore, in your case Mr. Karnavas would lead you through the examination-in-chief, in question-and-answer format. The rules further require that cross-examination is permitted for each witness; accordingly, both the Jokic Defence and the Prosecution would be permitted to ask you questions. Under Rule 90(H)(i), cross-examination can cover any evidence which you may be in a position to provide that is relevant to the Prosecution's case. Of course, you may invoke your right to remain silent on certain questions if you believe that the answer may have negative consequences for you. But this could possibly lead to, in some circumstances, less favourable consideration of that aspect of testimony by the Trial Chamber when it assesses your testimony. Finally, the Trial Chamber may ask you questions following your testimony. You should be warned that any incriminating testimony you give may be used against you. Mr. Blagojevic, do you have any questions? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is precisely because I believe that I could personally present my work and my actions and how I went about carrying out my work in the geographical area and at the time under consideration, because I believe there were no infractions of the regulations that were then in force in the area --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, for interrupting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry for you interrupting. We must insist that he not go into anything factual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course. I quite understand you. Shall we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Blagojevic, now that you have been informed of the three options available to you, this Trial Chamber requires you that you meet with Mr. Karnavas to discuss each option in detail and to determine which option is best for you in the current circumstances of your case. We noticed that you said you will obey whatever decisions this Trial Chamber will make. In addition to meeting with Mr. Karnavas to discuss the option available to you, if you choose option two, to make an unsworn statement, the Trial Chamber urges you that you and Mr. Karnavas discuss the contents of your proposed amendment before it is delivered in the courtroom. If you choose option three, as Mr. Karnavas will be leading you through your examination-in-chief and preparing you for cross-examination, the Trial Chamber requires that you meet with Mr. Karnavas at any time and as many times as is necessary to ensure that you are fully and sufficiently prepared to come before this Trial Chamber as a witness. You have expressed concern about the date of 30th July. While the Trial Chamber hopes to finish both Defence cases by this date, it is possible to hear you under whichever option you may choose at a later date, probably in September. This would give you and Mr. Karnavas sufficient time to meet, discuss the options, and prepare for either your statement or your testimony, if you choose either of those options. Your case is scheduled to close on the 25th of June. By 7th July, the Trial Chamber would like to be informed about the first meeting between you and your counsel have taken place. This is a decision of this Trial Chamber on that subject issue. Well -- yes, Mr. Blagojevic. THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] I do not wish to meet with him at any price. I do not wish to meet Karnavas at all. Your Honours, this is how I feel. That's why I said what I said. Bearing that in mind, do not force me to meet Karnavas. Make any ruling you wish. I cannot interfere in that, but I do not wish to meet Karnavas ever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, I'm not going to argue with you. A decision is a decision. I think both parties should respect a ruling by the Trial Chamber. This is all I could say at this stage. Well, is there anything else? Yes. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. One issue. It's come to my attention that there was a newspaper article written that I discussed briefly with Mr. Karnavas where the journalist said he has recently interviewed Mr. Karnavas. There are some unfortunate statements in there made by the journalist, and I would like the Court to be able to have those -- the article - there's a previous article by the same journalist - to review. I've suggested to Mr. Karnavas that we just agree that it's a good idea that we don't give interviews regarding the facts of the case during the case, and that perhaps that will resolve the issue. But I think the Court should see the articles and of course they are media articles, so I think we can take them with a grain of salt. But I think after giving it some thought and discussing the matter and receiving directions, I need to provide those materials to the Court for their review. But, as I said, I think Mr. Karnavas and I have had a chance to talk about it and perhaps this -- we won't have to deal with a problem like this again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Well, should we go to private session? Yes, we'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, is there anything else that the parties would like to mention? It seems to me there are none, so the hearing is adjourned.
